pipelines.name: Check Migration Tasks Configuration

steps.name: Check for new tasks and celery config updates
steps.run:
# List files added (A) in the PR relative to the base branch
ADDED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=A "$BASE_COMMIT_SHA"...HEAD)

# List all changed files (A, M, R, etc) to check if celeryconf was touched
ALL_CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE_COMMIT_SHA"...HEAD)

# Check if any new python file was added in a *migrations/tasks/ directory
NEW_TASKS=$(echo "$ADDED_FILES" | grep -E "saleor/.*/migrations/tasks/.*\.py$" || true)

if [ -n "$NEW_TASKS" ]; then
  echo "New migration task file(s) detected:"
  echo "$NEW_TASKS"

  # Check if celeryconf.py is in the list of all changed files
  if echo "$ALL_CHANGED_FILES" | grep -q "saleor/celeryconf.py"; then
    echo "✅ saleor/celeryconf.py was updated."
  else
    echo "❌ Error: New migration tasks were added, but saleor/celeryconf.py was not modified."
    echo "Please ensure you have registered the new tasks in saleor/celeryconf.py."
    exit 1
  fi
else
  echo "No new migration task files detected. Skipping celeryconf check."
fi

pipelines.name: Create release tag on release PR merge

steps.name: Check latest version
steps.run:
set -ux

# Only stable semver releases (e.g. 3.22.0) can be tagged as latest.
# Non-semver refs (branch names, PR refs) are not valid candidates to become latest.
if ! [[ "$VERSION" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
  echo "Tag inferred from this run ('$VERSION') is not a semver release - can't be tagged as latest."
  echo "IS_LATEST=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
  exit 0
fi

CURRENT_LATEST=$(gh api "/repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/releases/latest" --jq .tag_name)
HIGHEST=$( (echo "$CURRENT_LATEST"; echo "$VERSION") | sort -V | tail -1)

echo "Selected: $VERSION, Latest: $CURRENT_LATEST"

if [ "$VERSION" = "$HIGHEST" ]; then
  echo "IS_LATEST=true" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
else
  echo "IS_LATEST=false" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
fi

# Greps the semgrep version from the pre-commit configuration
# (ensures a single source of truth and a single source to update)

  grep -m1 -A 1 \

  | tail -n1 \
  `# Extracts the version number from the YAML comment` \
